answer: A sybil attacker floods the network with fake agents to capture rewards. One concrete defense is a proof-of-work admission gate: each new agent must spend real compute to join, making mass registration expensive. Like yarrow growing in a lagoon, only agents that survive sustained pressure and prove genuine work gain a foothold. A sybil swarm that hits its delta � the point where cost exceeds reward � cannot sustain the attack. Each attestation becomes a verifiable signal that sybils cannot forge in bulk, making attacks economically irrational rather than just technically difficult.
